name: process-solvents
licence: CC0-1.0 (public domain dedication) — first-party content compiled in this repository
retrieved_from: Hand-compiled in this repository from publicly published reference values: physical constants as tabulated in the NIST Chemistry WebBook and standard handbooks, Antoine constants in the NIST form log10(P/bar) = A - B/(T/K + C) together with the temperature range the NIST WebBook publishes each set as fitted over (antoine_tmin_k / antoine_tmax_k), Hansen solubility parameters from the published Hansen tables, ICH Q3C(R8) classes and residual-solvent limits, and GHS/CLP hazard classes. Nothing is fetched at runtime and no address here is read by any code.
description: 44 solvents used in pharmaceutical and fine-chemical process R&D, with the properties a process decision turns on: boiling and melting point, density, closed-cup flash point, dielectric constant, Hansen parameters, water miscibility, peroxide-forming tendency, ICH Q3C class and limit, an indicative greenness band, and the GHS hazard flags behind it. Antoine constants are carried for 16 solvents, each with the range it was fitted over, and validated against their own boiling points by tests/test_dataset.py; outside that range, and for the rest of the table, a Clausius-Clapeyron estimate answers and every result labels itself as such. Changed in 0.2.0: acetic acid gained the NIST Antoine set (its boiling-point dHvap is suppressed by vapour-phase dimerisation, so extrapolating it to ambient read 5.6x high); dimethyl carbonate's Hansen polar term was corrected from 8.6 to the published 3.9. VERIFY AGAINST A PRIMARY SOURCE before any value here enters a regulatory filing, a safety case, or equipment sizing: this is a working table for an agent's reasoning, not a certified reference.
